_README: Copy this file to roles_config.json and fill in the real values.
EVERY id, name and mapping below is a PLACEHOLDER. null means 'not supplied yet' —
the system disables the dependent synchronization path instead of guessing.
Secrets (ROLES_TOKEN, ROVER_API_KEY, ROBLOX_API_KEY) do NOT belong here.
They go in config.json / environment variables like every other secret in this project.
Any key starting with an underscore is ignored by the loader, so notes are safe to leave in.
_ranks_README: 14 normal ranks (Training Associate .. Branch Head) + a 15th Owner/CEO rank, plus special ranks.
key                    stable internal id, UPPERCASE, never shown to users
display                the exact string in the column F dropdown
category               HIGH-RANK | MID-RANK | LOW-RANK
order                  higher = more senior. Drives sorting AND rank comparison in permissions.
special                false for the 15 normal ranks, true for special ranks
special_group_order    groups special ranks together in the sort (all Overseers, then all Ambassadors)
main_discord_role_id   primary role id in the main server
main_aux_discord_role_ids  extra MAIN-SERVER-ONLY roles this rank also grants.
Auxiliary roles are never applied in branch servers.
They are managed, so obsolete ones are removed on a rank change.
roblox_roles_by_branch { BRANCH_KEY: roblox_group_role_id }.
ADDITIVE, not alternatives. The "N/A" entry is the BASELINE and is
ALWAYS applied. A branch entry is applied ON TOP of it, so a member
of ECHELON receives both the N/A role and the ECHELON role.
An empty object means this rank has NO Roblox equivalent.
Applied with Open Cloud assignRole / unassignRole, so a member can
hold several roles in one group at once. Only roles configured here
are ever unassigned — anything granted for another reason survives.
Every change is verified by re-reading the membership, because a key
without group:write can return 200 without applying anything.
Optional per-entry form, if a branch role lives in a different group:
"ECHELON": { "role_id": 1, "group_id": 12345 }
or set branches.<KEY>.roblox_group_id once for that whole branch.
syncs_roblox           defaults to true for normal ranks, false for special ranks.
_branches_README: One entry per branch, plus the required N/A entry for users with no branch.
discord_guild_id       that branch's own Discord server
discord_roles_by_rank  { RANK_KEY: role_id } applied inside that branch server
main_aux_discord_role_ids  MAIN-SERVER-ONLY roles granted by belonging to this branch.
This is the branch half of the auxiliary mapping: it lives in the
MAIN server, not the branch server, so a member's branch is visible
in the one server everybody is in. Managed, so the old branch's
auxiliary roles come off automatically on a branch change.
Valid on N/A too, if unaffiliated members should carry a role.
_default_registration_rank_README: Rank key given to a new record by /register — presumably Training Associate.
Left null on purpose: a new record gets a blank rank, which sorts to the bottom
of its section and synchronizes nothing, rather than a guessed starting rank.

discord._comment: main_guild_id is the designated server where /register is used.

_registration_README: OAUTH : Roblox OAuth 2.0 (default). Asks the user directly — no third-party opt-in.
ROVER : legacy Rover lookup. Requires each user to opt in to Rover's data sharing.
OAUTH needs, in the environment: ROBLOX_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, ROBLOX_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
and, below, a redirect_uri matching one registered on the Roblox app.
NOTE: a new Roblox OAuth app starts in PRIVATE mode, capped at 10 unique users,
until Roblox approves it for public mode. Submit it for review before rollout.

roblox_oauth._comment: Must exactly match a redirect URL registered on the Roblox OAuth app. Plain HTTPS (or http://localhost for local debugging), max 256 chars.
roblox_oauth._state_ttl_comment: How long an unfinished verification link stays valid, in seconds.

rover._comment: Legacy fallback, only used when registration.verification_method is ROVER.

_permissions_README: NOTHING IS PERMITTED UNTIL IT IS LISTED HERE. Unconfigured permissions deny.
CONDITIONS INSIDE ONE GRANT ARE ANDed:
allowed_relations   any of SELF, LOWER, EQUAL, HIGHER, UNRANKED — the relation of
the TARGET user to the ACTING user, compared by rank 'order'.
min_rank_order      optional floor on the acting user's rank order
allowed_categories  optional restriction on the acting user's CATEGORY
So { allowed_relations: [SELF], allowed_categories: [HIGH-RANK] } means
'only a HIGH-RANK, and only on themselves' — NOT 'anyone on themselves'.
GRANTS ARE ORed. To express 'anyone on themselves, OR a high rank on someone
below them', use two grants — the action is allowed if ANY of them matches:
"SET_STATUS": {
"grants": [
{ "allowed_relations": ["SELF"] },
{ "allowed_relations": ["LOWER"], "allowed_categories": ["HIGH-RANK"] }
The first grant has no category condition, so ANY registered member passes it
for themselves. The second only passes for a HIGH-RANK acting on someone of
lower rank. Add "EQUAL" to the second grant's relations if high ranks should
also be able to act on each other.
The flat shape (no "grants" key) is still accepted and means a single grant.
bootstrap_discord_ids  bypasses all rank checks. Needed to configure the system
before anyone has a rank. Prune once real ranks exist.
Rules with an empty allowed_relations are UNCONFIGURED and deny everyone —
that is deliberate, not an oversight. The real hierarchy has not been supplied,
and a guess here would silently grant real authority.

REGISTER_SELF.note: Anyone unregistered may register themselves. Safe to enable now.

VIEW_RECORD.note: decide who may view other users' records.

SET_TIMEZONE._shape_note: Two-grant example: anyone on themselves, OR a HIGH-RANK on someone below them.
SET_TIMEZONE.note: confirm whether high ranks should be able to set another user's timezone at all.

SET_RANK.note: high ranks only. Supply allowed_relations (likely LOWER) and a min_rank_order.

SET_BRANCH.note: high ranks only. Same shape as SET_RANK.

SET_STATUS.note: users may set their own allowed status; high ranks may set lower-ranked users'. Fill the first grant with ["SELF"] and the second with ["LOWER"] to enable that.

SET_LOA.note: pending the LOA data format definition. See roles/loa.py.

RESTRUCTURE_SHEET.note: who may trigger a full sheet re-layout.

ADMIN_INSPECT.note: who may inspect sync queue / dead letters.

sync._enabled_comment: Set false for a dry run: changes are computed and logged but not applied.
_removal_README: A record does not vanish from the sheet on its own. If it is deleted, the person
is no longer personnel: their managed Discord roles are stripped in the main server
AND every branch server, and re-entry requires /register again.
Roblox is handled the same way, via unassignRole:
UNASSIGN : unassign every managed role in every managed group (default)
SET_ROLE : unassign the managed roles, then leave removal_roblox_role_id behind
in the main group as a 'removed' marker
Built-in roles (Owner/Member/Guest) are never touched, so a stripped member falls
back to plain Member rather than being removed from the group.
sync._manage_status_formatting_comment: Installs conditional-format rules on column J. Off by default so it never clobbers hand-made rules.
